title: Road & Crossing Safety
strapline: Stop, look, listen — hold my hand at the kerb — and let's cross the road safely, just like we do out on a real walk.
intent: Knowing how to be safe near roads is genuinely important, potentially life-saving knowledge for young children, and building it through play means it sticks without ever being frightening.
The lollipop person, the crossing and the traffic lights introduce the community helpers and systems that keep everyone safe on busy streets.
Setting up a road, driving, walking and crossing is active, purposeful play — steering, stopping, waiting, looking, moving on gross-motor and self-regulation together.
The theme is full of mathematics — traffic light sequences, counting cars, positional language, fast and slow, stop and go.
Waiting, watching and following the rules of the road builds crucial self-regulation, listening and impulse control.
Real safety vocabulary and knowledge grow — kerb, crossing, traffic light, stop, look, listen, pavement, safe.
implementation: Build a road outdoors with chalk or tape — a crossing, traffic lights, a pavement — and bring in bikes, trikes, prams and a lollipop sign.
Play both drivers and pedestrians, and model the crossing routine every time: 'Stop at the kerb. Look and listen. No cars? Now we can cross.'
Take a role — the lollipop person, a driver who must stop at red — so children practise the real rules in a safe, repeatable way.
Bring in maths through the play — sequence the red-amber-green lights, count the cars waiting, use positional and speed words as you move.
Weave the real knowledge in warmly on every actual walk — holding hands at the kerb, stopping, looking, listening — so the play and real life connect.
Extend with a traffic-light game (green go, red freeze) for self-regulation, and let children take the responsible roles of crossing patrol and traffic controller.
key_questions: Stop at the kerb — look and listen. Any cars? Is it safe to cross now?
What order do the traffic lights go in — red, amber, green?
How many cars are waiting at the crossing?
What does the lollipop person do to keep us safe?
Which is going fast, and which is going slow?

impact.text: Children build life-saving road-safety knowledge through play so it sticks without ever being frightening.
Children meet the community helpers and systems that keep everyone safe on busy streets.
Children wait, watch and follow the rules of the road, building self-regulation and impulse control.
Children sequence the traffic lights, count the cars and use positional and speed words.
Children gain real safety vocabulary — kerb, crossing, traffic light, stop, look, listen.

enhancements: A chalk or tape road outdoors with a crossing, traffic lights and a pavement.
Bikes, trikes, prams and a lollipop sign for drivers and pedestrians.
A traffic-light game — green go, red freeze — for self-regulation.
The crossing routine practised warmly on every real walk.
Responsible roles — crossing patrol, traffic controller — for the children to take.

playing_exploring: Children play out being drivers, walkers and crossing helpers, exploring the busy world of the road safely.
They test steering, stopping and moving with their bodies and wheeled toys.
active_learning: Children practise the crossing routine again and again, taking the safety rules seriously and getting them right.
creating_thinking: Children work out the sequence of the lights and when it is safe to cross, applying real safety knowledge to their play.
